recipe: Configure ESLint rules in your `.eslintrc.js` file to identify and prevent common errors, ensuring code correctness and promoting consistency throughout the codebase.
trigger_condition: When setting up or maintaining code quality standards in a React or JavaScript project.
evidence: By configuring rules in the `.eslintrc.js` file, ESLint helps identify and prevent common errors, ensuring code correctness and promoting consistency throughout the codebase.

recipe: Enable the 'format on save' feature in your IDE so code is automatically formatted according to rules set in the `.prettierrc` configuration file, and integrate Prettier with ESLint to handle formatting alongside coding standards.
trigger_condition: When you need consistent code formatting across your project and want automatic feedback on code issues.
evidence: By enabling the "format on save" feature in your IDE, code is automatically formatted according to the rules set in the `.prettierrc` configuration file.

recipe: When refactoring a TypeScript project, prioritize updating type declarations first, then resolve TypeScript errors throughout the project.
trigger_condition: When performing large refactoring processes in a TypeScript codebase where runtime data issues may go unnoticed.
evidence: When refactoring, prioritize updating type declarations first, then resolving TypeScript errors throughout the project.

recipe: Use Husky to run linting, code formatting, and type checking before each commit to ensure no faulty commits are pushed to the repository.
trigger_condition: When you want to enforce code quality gates at the commit stage of your git workflow.
evidence: Husky enables you to perform various tasks such as linting, code formatting, and type checking before allowing code pushes.

recipe: Always configure and use absolute imports with the `@/*` path alias mapping to `./src/*`, so that files can be moved freely without breaking import paths.
trigger_condition: When organizing file imports in a React or TypeScript project to avoid messy relative paths like `../../../component`.
evidence: Absolute imports should always be configured and used because it makes it easier to move files around and avoid messy import paths such as `../../../component`.

recipe: Enforce kebab-case naming for all files and folders (excluding `__tests__`) using ESLint's `check-file/filename-naming-convention` and `check-file/folder-naming-convention` rules.
trigger_condition: When establishing naming conventions to keep a codebase consistent and easier to navigate.
evidence: you can enforce that all files should be named in `kebab-case`. This can help you to keep your codebase consistent and easier to navigate.
